entry.title: Report: Claude Code sends users' email addresses in User-Agent headers during web searches, raising privacy concerns [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Users have reported that Claude Code includes their email addresses in the User-Agent request headers when performing web searches, exposing this information to third-party websites without consent. This behavior has led to increased scam emails and privacy violations, prompting some users to switch to alternative AI tools. The issue was raised on GitHub, where developers noted that a built-in privacy plugin was introduced in version 2.1.317 to block this behavior by default, though users are encouraged to report any gaps in its effectiveness.

entry.title: Mark Cuban says Meta knowingly runs AI deepfake scam ads generating $16 billion in fraud-linked revenue, internal documents reveal [ ! ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Mark Cuban accused Meta of knowingly allowing AI-generated deepfake scam ads on Facebook that target vulnerable users, including older adults, resulting in significant financial losses. Internal Meta documents revealed the company expected about $16 billion in revenue from ads linked to scams and prohibited products in 2024, with users seeing around 15 billion high-risk ads daily. Meta's internal safety staff estimated its platforms contribute to a third of successful scams in the U.S., with automated systems only banning advertisers when there is a 95% likelihood of fraud. Meta disputed the documents' portrayal, citing a 58% drop in scam ad complaints and removal of over 134 million scam ads in 2025. Older Americans reported losing $7.7 billion to internet crimes in 2025, with AI-related scams accounting for over $352 million in losses among reported cases. Cuban urged caution when encountering ads featuring famous faces and recommended verifying products for scams, especially to protect older family members. The FBI encourages reporting suspected scams promptly to aid in recovery efforts, though many victims do not file complaints.

entry.title: Researcher expresses skepticism about the ingenuity of current autonomous AI R&D based on observed limitations in side projects and model performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A researcher shared doubts about the perceived ingenuity of autonomous AI research and development after monitoring several side projects, including building a Scrabble engine, an Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe bot, and AI philosophy research. They observed that AI models often showed poor judgment, such as failing to identify key literature, conducting uninformative experiments, and pursuing trivial directions in complex tasks. The researcher noted that improvements often came from human guidance and steering rather than the models' autonomous innovation. They highlighted challenges like models producing difficult-to-understand reports and the need for iterative prompting to achieve better results. This skepticism contrasts with some hill-climbing tasks where AI showed more effective progress under directed effort.

entry.title: Thinking Machines launches Inkling 2 Small, a 594B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with vision input and improved agentic coding, available on Tinker with weights to be open-sourced after safety review [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Thinking Machines introduced Inkling 2 Small, its second-generation AI model featuring 594 billion total parameters and 17 billion active parameters, supporting image inputs and variable effort. The model surpasses previous versions in coding, vision, knowledge work, and reasoning, achieving a score of 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. Initially available through the Tinker platform with closed weights, the full model weights are planned for release under an Apache 2.0 license following external safety testing and red-teaming. Inkling 2 Small was trained with reinforcement learning on extensive long-horizon coding and autoresearch tasks, improving instruction following, verification, and usability in agent loops. It incorporates a 292M-parameter vision encoder enabling strong visual capabilities such as OCR and visual reasoning, and it demonstrated superior performance in tasks like wine identification from images. The model supports fine-tuning and sampling on Tinker, with downloadable checkpoints to be provided alongside the open weights release.

entry.title: Tesla cancels Cybertruck project as Elon Musk shifts company focus to robotics and artificial intelligence [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Tesla has decided to discontinue its Cybertruck project as CEO Elon Musk redirects the company's priorities toward robotics and artificial intelligence development. This move signals a strategic shift in Tesla's investment toward advancing automation and AI technologies.

entry.title: Ask HN: How are investors adjusting strategies amid the AI market bubble decline? [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]

Participants share varied perspectives on shifting investments toward alternative technologies and responding to evolving market conditions.

entry.title: Nasdaq falls 5.5% for worst day in 19 months as investors anticipate AI regulation after Democratic election wins [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The Nasdaq composite index dropped 5.5%, marking its worst day in 19 months and entering correction territory with over $2 trillion wiped off its value. The decline followed Democratic victories in US midterm elections, which raised investor concerns about potential regulatory restrictions on AI datacenter expansions and technology sector growth. Chip stocks led the sell-off, with companies like SanDisk and Western Digital falling sharply, while the VIX volatility index surged 61%. The downturn extended to Asian markets, reflecting global investor anxiety about the future pace of AI development amid expected political hurdles. Analysts noted that Democratic control could slow datacenter buildouts and increase legislative challenges for AI and tech industries in the coming years.

entry.title: Google donates Agent Substrate and gVisor to CNCF to support scalable, secure AI agent orchestration [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
entry.summary: Google has contributed its Agent Substrate and gVisor projects to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) to foster community collaboration and development within the cloud native ecosystem. Agent Substrate is designed to efficiently manage AI agents by separating stateful actors from compute workers, addressing challenges like idle resource waste and control plane overload that traditional Kubernetes cannot handle. Agent Substrate enables AI agents to maintain state while minimizing resource use during idle periods and supports rapid wake-up times under 500 milliseconds. Google announced this donation at KubeCon North America 2026, marking these projects as Sandbox-level CNCF initiatives aimed at advancing secure, scalable AI agent infrastructure.

entry.summary: Anthropic, an AI research company, is rapidly advancing its artificial intelligence technologies by accelerating the development of its Claude model amid ongoing industry discussions advocating for a slowdown in AI progress. The company continues to prioritize innovation while addressing safety and ethical concerns associated with AI development.

entry.title: NYU Professor Aswath Damodaran warns of potential AI market bubble and urges cautious investment amid inflated valuations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: NYU Professor Aswath Damodaran discusses concerns about overvaluation in the artificial intelligence sector, suggesting that current market enthusiasm may resemble a bubble. He highlights the need for careful investment decisions and critical evaluation of AI companies to mitigate financial risks associated with inflated expectations.

entry.title: Democratic congressional victory may increase AI regulation in US, potentially slowing growth and aiding China's AI ambitions [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A Democratic sweep in the US Congress is expected to lead to tighter regulatory scrutiny of artificial intelligence and the data centers that support it. This shift follows concerns about AI contributing to political backlash against the Republican Party and President Donald Trump, who had been a supporter of the tech industry. Increased regulation could slow AI development in the US, potentially giving China an advantage in advancing its AI capabilities amid reduced competition.

entry.title: Anthropic publishes study on researchers using Claude AI for data analysis and writing across scientific fields, highlighting potential to accelerate discovery [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic researchers analyzed 207,000 sessions of Claude AI use in scientific research to understand how it supports tasks like data analysis and writing, with heavier use in formal sciences such as computer science and mathematics. The study found that while Claude is less used for idea generation and data gathering, specialized AI tools could increase its role in these areas. The report suggests that widespread adoption of current AI capabilities could double research output in some fields, with potential increases up to 15-fold in computer science and statistics if AI handles all non-physical research tasks. Researchers surveyed expect AI models to conduct full research projects independently by 2030, indicating significant future impacts on the pace of scientific discovery.

entry.title: Palo Alto Networks in talks to acquire AI agent security startup Clutch for $500 million, valuing it at about 50 times ARR [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Palo Alto Networks is negotiating to buy Clutch Security, a startup that secures AI agents' access to company systems, for $500 million in cash plus milestone payments. Clutch was last valued at $85 million in early 2025 and is approaching $10 million in annual recurring revenue, indicating a valuation of roughly 50 times ARR if the deal completes. This potential acquisition would be Palo Alto Networks' seventh this year as it responds to rising AI-driven cyberattacks by acquiring innovative startups rather than building in-house. Clutch's competitors have also been acquired recently, reflecting growing market interest in securing AI agent access to systems amid increasing cybersecurity threats.

entry.title: AI coding agents transform software development workflows in 2026, enabling task delegation across multiple files and layers [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: In 2026, AI coding agents have become mainstream tools that can inspect code repositories, modify multiple files, execute commands, run tests, and iterate autonomously, shifting developer workflows from line-by-line assistance to delegating complete tasks. Surveys from JetBrains and Stack Overflow show widespread adoption, with 68% to 73% of developers using AI agents daily. These agents improve productivity by handling repetitive and predictable tasks across coding, testing, and project planning, while developers focus on defining requirements, reviewing changes, and ensuring architectural fit. The evolving role of AI in software development emphasizes orchestration and collaboration rather than full automation, reflecting changes in required developer skills and workflows.

entry.title: InfoQ Architecture & Design: Enterprise IAM requires identity as a core architectural element beyond authentication, emphasizing data models, access relationships, and revocation policies
entry.summary: The article argues that identity management must be integrated into enterprise architecture rather than treated as an afterthought, especially in regulated environments where auditability of access is critical. It highlights that traditional role-based access control (RBAC) models fall short when managing complex relationships like ownership and validity of service accounts, advocating for graph-based models to better represent these connections. Drawing from experience in financial services, the article discusses how designing identity as part of the data model enables precise queries about access history and ownership, which are essential for compliance audits. It also covers practical governance challenges such as managing service account owners during personnel changes and reducing revocation latency by merging attestation, rotation, and vaulting workflows into a unified process. The piece underscores that identity design decisions impact service boundaries and event flows, requiring architectural consideration to ensure security and compliance at scale. It advises organizations to record every access grant and revocation as timestamped events to facilitate audit queries and maintain consistent security postures across distributed systems.

entry.title: Cisco assigns former startup founder to rewrite 98% of its legacy code using AI within 24 months with unlimited AI resources [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Cisco president Jeetu Patel has tasked Padmanabhan Krishnamurthy, a 27-year-old ex-startup founder, with refactoring 98% of the company's legacy code in two years using AI, providing him unlimited AI tokens to accelerate the process. Krishnamurthy joined Cisco after its acquisition of his translation startup and was previously underutilized in a low-level role. Patel aims to inject fresh ideas and challenge the status quo by combining experienced operators with AI-native engineers like Krishnamurthy. While AI coding adoption is rising rapidly, Patel acknowledges potential friction between younger and veteran employees but believes this tension can drive innovation. The initiative reflects Cisco's broader strategy to modernize its software infrastructure leveraging AI capabilities.

entry.title: Grafista develops AI design tool that eliminates text prompts by using visual references to simplify graphic design for non-experts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Grafista is building an AI graphic design tool that removes the need for text prompts, aiming to help users without design or prompt engineering skills create professional-looking designs. The tool replaces traditional chatbot interfaces with visual inputs to guide the AI, addressing challenges users face with prompt-based design tools that often produce repetitive or mediocre results. The company argues that while chatbots have simplified user interfaces, they require users to learn effective prompting, which can be difficult and time-consuming, especially for complex tasks like graphic design. By focusing on visual references instead of text commands, Grafista aims to streamline the design process and produce more unique, high-quality outputs without requiring advanced skills.

entry.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Small (17A-594B), trained on 12 trillion tokens in 68 hours, outperforming Muse Spark [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Small, a 594 billion parameter multimodal mixture-of-experts model trained from scratch on 12 trillion tokens over 68 hours. The model supports text and image input with text output and features a 1 million token context window. It is currently available on the Tinker platform, with Apache 2.0 open weights expected after external safety testing. Inkling 2 Small is noted for its competitive performance against similar-sized Chinese models and Western counterparts like Mistral and Meta Muse. The training utilized native NVFP4 precision and included a reinforcement learning phase. The model emphasizes customizability and fine-tuning efficiency, positioning it as a leading open-weight model developed outside China according to current rankings.

entry.title: Linum.ai releases Pyramid-JiT text-to-image model trained for $21K with Apache 2.0 licensed weights [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Linum.ai, a two-person research lab, has released the Pyramid-JiT (P-JiT) text-to-image model trained for approximately $21,000, offering an experimental open-source model under the Apache 2.0 license. The model uses a novel architecture that compresses image tokens more aggressively than typical approaches, enabling faster training and inference with fewer samples compared to previous versions. The P-JiT model operates in pixel space and integrates a frozen Qwen3.5-4B text encoder with a diffusion-based image generator, achieving a 32×32 token reduction that significantly lowers computational costs. This release serves as a proof of concept toward Linum.ai's broader goal of developing efficient generative video models that democratize animation creation by making inference faster and cheaper.

entry.title: Google open-sources Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin to scale design-driven AI software development with context-rich and stateless AI sessions [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Google has released the Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin as open source under the Apache 2.0 license to support design-driven AI software development. The framework uses "Elephant" sessions for long-term architectural design and "Goldfish" sessions for stateless validation, aiming to improve code reliability by aligning human system comprehension with AI execution. The plugin automates the development lifecycle by managing context transfer between design and validation phases, guiding developers through brainstorming, drafting detailed design documents, and adversarial review by multiple AI instances. Thousands of Google engineers use this tool internally to ship production code, and the open-source release includes customizable workflows and integration support for various development environments. This approach addresses the risks of increased coding speed without sufficient guardrails by emphasizing structured design and validation, potentially reducing bugs and improving software quality in AI-assisted development workflows.

entry.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with 15-second video clips, 30% lower cost, and improved editing and consistency [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Google DeepMind has released Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, an update to its video generation model that supports native 15-second clips, multi-turn conversational editing, and enhanced adherence to visual references. The new version reduces costs by 30% compared to its predecessor and is available through the Gemini API and Google Cloud for professional video production. The update allows users to create longer videos with precise control over duration and improved consistency in characters, objects, and scenes across frames. It also enables faster editing through conversational prompts without needing to regenerate entire clips. Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash supports clearer lip-sync and more natural multi-speaker dialogue, making it suitable for creating branded ads, virtual try-ons, and social media content at scale.

entry.title: Meta launches Muse Voice video chat feature with customizable AI avatars for US users ahead of Muse Charm wearable release [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Meta has introduced Muse Voice, enabling US users to video chat with their customizable Muse AI avatars using new real-time avatar and voice technologies. The avatars, which can resemble people, animals, or other characters, respond with expressions and gestures matching the conversation tone, though they do not see users. This feature, available on mobile, web, and Mac platforms, precedes Meta's planned launch of a Tamagotchi-like Muse Charm wearable device that will display the avatar and allow live interaction. Meta aims to enhance user connection with AI agents through these anthropomorphic avatars and real-time conversations.

entry.title: Pair Flow launches VS Code extension to let developers review and approve AI-generated code changes incrementally [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Pair Flow has introduced a Visual Studio Code extension designed to help developers maintain control over AI-generated code by breaking changes into small, understandable chunks that require explicit approval before being applied. The extension stores proposed changes locally without modifying source files until approved, supports multiple AI providers, and emphasizes transparency and safety by rejecting unsafe paths and preventing automatic execution of shell commands. The tool aims to keep developers in the reasoning loop by pausing before each code change and providing explanations for every modification, allowing users to inspect diffs side by side. It stores API keys securely using VS Code SecretStorage and does not include any hosted services or product analytics, ensuring privacy and control over the coding process.

entry.title: Cult.fit uses OpenAI Codex to accelerate tool development and improve operational workflows across teams
entry.summary: Cult.fit is leveraging OpenAI's Codex to enable teams across different functions to build custom tools more quickly and transform their work processes. This adoption aims to enhance operational efficiency and agility within the company by integrating AI-assisted coding into daily workflows.

entry.title: Tinyfish.ai shares lessons from building a deep research system that iteratively searches, browses, and synthesizes web data into long-form reports with citations [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Tinyfish.ai developed a deep research system designed to investigate topics by searching the web, browsing sites, gathering evidence from multiple sources, and producing detailed reports with citations. The project revealed that challenges centered more on context management, orchestration, and product design than on research itself. The system architecture includes an orchestrator that plans and executes research by invoking tools like search and browsing, continuously refining understanding and generating partial reports for users. Initially, the system separated planning and execution into distinct components, but this caused issues with maintaining context across iterative research cycles. The orchestrator accumulated understanding over time, while the planner operated with limited context, leading to inconsistencies in follow-up queries. To address this, planning was integrated into the orchestrator's reasoning loop, preserving context and improving coherence. The experience highlights the costs of information boundaries in multi-component AI systems and the importance of unified reasoning processes for reliable agent design.

entry.title: Australian universities integrate ChatGPT and AI tools into curricula to prepare students for AI-driven workforce [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Australian universities are expanding access to ChatGPT and incorporating AI technologies into teaching and learning to equip students with skills needed for an AI-enabled workforce. This initiative aims to create graduates who are proficient in AI applications relevant to future job markets.

entry.title: Coforge joins SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network to collaborate on Grok AI platform [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Coforge has joined the SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network to collaborate on Grok, an advanced artificial intelligence initiative. This partnership leverages Coforge's expertise to support the development and deployment of AI technologies associated with SpaceX's Grok platform.

entry.title: Obelisk Club reports 9.8% of top-charting App Store apps mention AI, with 26.7% of free apps offering in-app purchases or subscriptions as of November 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Obelisk Club analyzed 178,637 apps appearing in the App Store top charts across 173 countries since October 2026, finding that nearly 10% mention AI-related terms and over a quarter of free apps monetize through in-app purchases or subscriptions. The study also revealed that 20.3% of these apps have not been updated for a year or more, and subscription pricing is the most common complaint in low-rated reviews. The report highlights that AI mentions are concentrated in Graphics & Design, Photo & Video, and Developer Tools categories, with apps selling in-app purchases or subscriptions being three times more likely to mention AI. Independent developers account for 67.3% of charting apps, maintaining similar ratings to larger publishers. The research will be updated quarterly to track trends such as AI adoption and app maintenance over time.

entry.title: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky launches AI lab, sells intellectual property to new venture for $7.1 million, with CTO also involved [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky has started a new AI lab and sold some intellectual property to this venture for $7.1 million in cash, as disclosed during Airbnb's third-quarter earnings report. The company also secured rights to invest in future equity financings of the lab and to license certain intellectual property for internal use. Airbnb's Chief Technology Officer Ahmad Al-Dahle holds equity in the AI lab and, like Chesky, provides services to the venture. This move reflects a growing trend of tech CEOs pursuing side projects alongside their primary executive roles.

entry.title: OpenAI ends use of NDAs with public officials for data center projects, commits to transparency and local community agreements [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI announced it will no longer use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials for its data center projects, responding to recent voter opposition to data center expansion. The company will limit confidentiality to legitimate security, trade secrets, or proprietary information and will establish local compacts reflecting community priorities for each new data center it operates. In addition to dropping NDAs, OpenAI pledged to cover the full electricity costs and infrastructure for its data centers, publish expected job creation figures, and report on hiring to support local communities. This move follows similar steps by Amazon and aims to increase transparency and address concerns about data center developments.

entry.title: Airbnb founder Brian Chesky self-funds secretive AI startup with potential Airbnb investment and technology licensing [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Airbnb disclosed new details about a stealth AI startup controlled and self-funded by its founder and CEO Brian Chesky, revealing a possible agreement for Airbnb to invest in the company and license its technology. Chesky has been financing the AI lab independently while continuing to lead Airbnb, which he founded nearly 20 years ago. Airbnb's Chief Technology Officer Ahmad Al-Dahle, who joined the company in January after working on AI at Meta, has been advising the startup. The information was partially revealed in a securities filing following Airbnb's quarterly report.

entry.title: Anthropic IPO could create hundreds of millionaires as CEO Dario Amodei expresses concerns about the company's mission [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic's planned initial public offering (IPO) is expected to generate significant wealth for hundreds of its employees, potentially making them millionaires. However, CEO Dario Amodei has voiced worries about the company's mission and its future direction. The IPO reflects Anthropic's growth and valuation in the AI industry, but Amodei's concerns highlight ongoing internal considerations about balancing business objectives with the company's foundational goals. These dynamics may influence Anthropic's strategic decisions following the public offering.

entry.title: Airbnb plans to launch an AI travel agent with a custom interface for trip planning in the first half of 2027 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Airbnb announced in its Q3 2026 shareholder letter that it is developing an AI travel agent designed to help users plan and book trips, aiming for a launch in early 2027. The company emphasized that this AI agent will offer a richer, travel-specific experience beyond simple chatbots, using a variety of interface elements like maps, photos, and itineraries to assist users. The AI agent will enable guests to explore options, collaborate with travel companions, and take actions directly within Airbnb's platform. Airbnb's CEO Brian Chesky has previously described the upcoming agent as having a more advanced interface than typical chatbots, reflecting the company's view that AI is significantly transforming its product development and operations.

entry.title: Airbnb plans to launch a personalized AI travel agent in the first half of 2027 to assist with trip planning, bookings, and support during stays [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Airbnb announced it will launch a custom AI travel agent in early 2027 designed to enhance the travel planning experience by offering a richer interface than typical chatbots. The agent will help users research destinations, compare accommodations, manage bookings, and provide assistance throughout their trips, including handling changes, payments, and safety support. The AI agent will leverage Airbnb's two decades of experience and use travel-specific interface components like maps, photos, and itineraries to create a personalized planning tool. Airbnb aims to maintain the aspirational and social aspects of travel planning while providing practical support beyond booking, with future expansions to include services and experiences.

entry.title: India's Coforge joins SpaceX partner network to deploy Grok AI enterprise tools [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: India-based IT services company Coforge has joined SpaceX's partner network to deploy Grok AI tools for enterprise customers. This collaboration aims to integrate Grok's AI capabilities into Coforge's offerings, enhancing AI-driven solutions for businesses. The partnership reflects growing industry efforts to expand AI tool adoption across enterprise sectors.

entry.title: Nvidia plans to retrofit old telecom buildings into AI data centers across 20 US states with Apollo Global Management [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Nvidia is exploring a faster way to deploy its chips by converting existing buildings owned by a struggling telecom company into small AI data centers. The chip designer has approached private equity firm Apollo Global Management to create a network of these data centers potentially spanning 20 states in the US, according to sources familiar with the effort.

entry.title: The Information: AI model efficiency gains may offset rising data center costs amid US expansion restrictions and local opposition [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: US election results have led to increased restrictions on data center expansion, raising concerns among tech executives and investors about higher costs for running AI workloads. Despite rising prices for Nvidia hardware and server rentals, AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic report significant efficiency improvements in their models, reducing per-task costs and potentially offsetting infrastructure constraints. Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman expressed optimism about continuing data center growth despite local resistance and project cancellations. However, investors showed mixed reactions, favoring established cloud providers over smaller ones awaiting approvals. The impact of regulatory backlash is expected to be more pronounced for data centers planned for 2028 and beyond, while AI firms with high profit margins may have room to lower prices to sustain demand.

entry.title: Perplexity launches Teammates, always-on AI agents for workspaces integrating with Perplexity Computer, requiring $200/month Max plan subscription [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Perplexity has introduced Teammates, its own version of always-on AI agents designed for workplace use, competing with OpenAI's Dots and Anthropic's Claude Duet. These agents can handle multiple roles simultaneously within a workspace, leveraging existing projects, skills, and memory from Perplexity's tools. Teammates work alongside Perplexity Computer, an AI system that deploys agents on user devices to complete tasks, but they extend capabilities by enabling collaboration on ongoing, large-scale work. Users can monitor Teammates' progress through individual threads in the Perplexity app and interact with them via Slack. Access to Teammates requires a subscription to Perplexity's $200 per month Max plan.

entry.title: Unity Software reports 32% revenue growth driven by AI-based ad business, shares rise 13% [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Unity Software reported a 32% increase in revenue, fueled by rapid growth in its AI-based advertising offering launched earlier this year, leading to a 13% jump in its shares. The company also projected a slightly faster growth rate for the fourth quarter. Unity, traditionally known for its gaming technology, is expanding its business through AI-driven advertising solutions.

entry.title: Anthropic launches personal finance feature for Claude with Plaid integration ahead of planned IPO [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic has introduced a personal finance feature for its AI chatbot Claude, allowing users to connect their bank accounts via Plaid for read-only access. This addition addresses one of the most requested use cases and comes as the company prepares for its planned initial public offering.

entry.title: Meta warns election-driven opposition to data centers may hinder AI infrastructure expansion amid growing community resistance [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Meta president Dina Powell McCormick said the Democratic wins in the recent midterm elections could make it harder for companies to build data centers, as political opposition and community pushback against these projects increase. She linked the backlash to broader public concerns about AI technology and emphasized the need for the industry to better communicate the benefits of data centers and AI. Meta has operated data centers in 23 states and plans several large projects, but Powell McCormick noted that future developments will face more scrutiny and require clear local benefits, such as supporting local labor and funding public services. Despite these challenges, Meta expects its investments in AI and data center compute capacity to remain valuable, with demand for leasing compute resources continuing to grow.

entry.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Cyber model for vulnerability hunting, finds hundreds of Linux and Firefox security issues amid rising AI-driven cyber threats [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI has released a new cybersecurity-focused AI model, ChatGPT Cyber, available to top-tier users in its Daybreak Red program for offensive security research. The model has already identified 948 potential vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel and 81 novel issues in Firefox, highlighting AI's growing role in both discovering and potentially exploiting software flaws. Security researchers using OpenAI's earlier GPT 5.6 Sol model found a severe Ubuntu server vulnerability, demonstrating how AI can rapidly uncover complex bugs that humans might miss. OpenAI is investing $1 billion to support cybersecurity professionals working on critical infrastructure, but experts warn that the pace of AI-driven vulnerability discovery may outstrip defenders' resources, especially as some AI tools are being restricted to limit misuse. While OpenAI dedicates significant compute power to pro bono vulnerability research, the scale of investment remains modest compared to other AI projects. The company emphasizes a narrow window for defenders to patch critical systems before AI capabilities become more accessible to malicious actors, underscoring the urgent need for expanded security efforts in the AI era.

entry.title: Anthropic publishes research on welfare consideration in multi-agent AI systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic's Alignment Science blog presents research exploring how AI systems with multiple agents can incorporate welfare considerations into their interactions. The study examines frameworks for ensuring that agents account for the well-being of others within multi-agent environments. This work contributes to the broader effort to align AI behavior with ethical and cooperative principles in complex systems.

entry.title: OpenAI president Greg Brockman says company could be IPO ready in 2027 as enterprise revenue grows [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman said the company could be ready for an initial public offering in 2027, citing strong growth in its enterprise revenue. Speaking at a Wall Street Journal tech conference, Brockman highlighted how OpenAI has gained ground in the enterprise market, where competitors like Anthropic had previously established a presence. Brockman noted that OpenAI's enterprise business has doubled and now accounts for the majority of its revenue, up from about 30% previously. He attributed the growth to sustained investments and partnerships with clients such as JPMorgan Chase. The company has shifted from being perceived mainly as a consumer-focused firm to a committed enterprise AI provider, emphasizing building trust and delivering measurable milestones for business customers.

entry.title: Anthropic launches Claude Personal Finance tool to analyze spending via Plaid-connected bank and card accounts in US beta [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic introduced a new Personal Finance feature for its AI assistant Claude, allowing users to connect their bank and credit card accounts through Plaid to ask questions about their finances. The tool provides read-only access to account data, enabling Claude to summarize spending, flag potential issues like duplicate charges, and explain financial concepts without managing or moving money. The Personal Finance tool aims to help users understand their spending patterns and financial status in everyday language, without ads or sponsored offers. It is currently rolling out in beta to Pro, Max, and Ultra plan users in the US, following similar features launched earlier by competitors like OpenAI's ChatGPT. Anthropic also ensures that conversations in the Personal Finance hub are not used to train its AI models.

entry.title: Meta launches voice conversations and expressive avatars for Muse AI agent in US iOS app, with plans for AI glasses and Muse Charm device
entry.summary: Meta has introduced a voice mode for its Muse AI agent, allowing real-time voice conversations accompanied by animated avatars that sync with speech. The feature is currently available on the Muse iOS app in the US, with users able to customize voice tones and avatar expressions. The voice mode responds quickly, though occasional pauses occur when the AI retrieves information.
